name: Recsys / personalization feature platforms
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: The recsys/personalization feature-platform segment is now thinner than it was a year ago. Independent vendors as of May 2026: (1) Chalk - the breakout incumbent for this slice; proprietary cloud SaaS, $50M Series A at $500M valuation May 2025 (Felicis lead, Triatomic Capital, General Catalyst, Unusual Ventures, Xfund); Compute Engine translates Python feature definitions to C++/Rust pipelines; explicit 'Search & Ranking' and 'Recommender Systems & Personalization' marketed use cases; Whatnot reference at 300M+ features/sec, P99 100 ms, 1 MB+ payloads, tens of thousands of features per ranking request; Apartment List reference at sub-5 ms feature retrieval. (2) Feast - Apache-2.0, Linux Foundation AI/Data Foundation governance, joined the PyTorch Ecosystem in 2025-2026; BYO-online-store (Redis, DynamoDB, Postgres, Snowflake); the ranking team is responsible for upstream Spark/Flink/dbt materialisation. (3) Hopsworks - AGPL-v3 open-core, RonDB-backed online tier (the 'world's fastest key-value store' per their marketing), 250k+ ops/sec at 7.5 ms p99, SIGMOD 2024 paper claiming 10x lower p99 than SageMaker/Vertex; Enterprise Edition behind a paid licence; ranking benchmarks largely from 2024 not 2025-2026. The four major exits/segment collapses are: Fennel acquired by Databricks April 17 2025 (Rust real-time engine, explicit 'personalized ranking and marketplace recommendations' positioning, Upwork/Cricut customers); Tecton acquired by Databricks August 22 2025 (~$900M reported value, ~$160M total raised, now embedded in Agent Bricks); Featureform acquired by Redis October 9 2025 and relaunched as Redis Feature Form April 20 2026 (workspaces/multi-tenancy/RBAC, targets 'fraud detection, risk scoring, personalization, recommendation systems'). The recsys-relevant in-house feature platforms (Whatnot was historically in-house then moved to Chalk; DoorDash Riviera + Redis ElastiCache; Pinterest Manas/TransAct V2 stack; Instacart Griffin 2.0; Netflix internal; Spotify internal; Meta DLRM/HSTU on bespoke parameter servers) are not vendor competitors but they set the architectural reference. Online KV stores used to build feature stores in-house specifically for ranking: Redis/ElastiCache (DoorDash, Instacart, Swiggy), Aerospike (Sony PlayStation, Adobe, Criteo, Wayfair, Myntra), DynamoDB, ScyllaDB, RonDB. Ranking-product (FS+scorer bundle) competitors: Metarank (open-source learn-to-rank with Redis state, 10-20 ms p99 reranking), Recombee, Algolia AI Recommendations, Amazon Personalize, Google Recommendations AI - these are not direct beava competitors but absorb buyers who would otherwise build.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Chalk owns the high-throughput live-commerce/marketplace recsys reference position. Whatnot - the lighthouse recsys customer - runs 300M+ features/sec at P99 100 ms (end-to-end 150 ms with 1 MB+ payloads, tens of thousands of features per ranking call), with feed-ranking driving 65 % of GMV and the For-You-Feed alone driving 50 % of GMV (Whatnot GMV ~$6B in 2025, up from ~$3B in 2024). Apartment List runs sub-5 ms feature retrieval for search ranking. Chalk's customer roster for ranking/recsys-adjacent workloads: Whatnot (live commerce ranking), Apartment List (search ranking), Medely (healthcare staffing matching), Sunrun (solar leads), MoneyLion, Iwoca (some are risk-adjacent rather than pure ranking). Hopsworks holds the EU/on-prem 'lakehouse + first-class feature store' position with Feldera+Hopsworks real-time fraud reference but a weaker public recsys reference. Feast is the BYO-substrate default for risk teams at PayPal-style operations and held the open-source default but is a fetch layer, not a compute layer. Funding/M&A 2025-2026: Chalk $50M Series A May 2025 ($500M valuation, Felicis lead); Tecton acquired by Databricks August 2025 ($900M-class value, $160M total raised); Fennel acquired by Databricks April 2025 (Rust engine, ex-Meta/Google Brain team); Featureform acquired by Redis October 2025, Redis Feature Form launched April 2026. Within twelve months the independent recsys-feature-platform segment contracted to three viable players (Chalk, Feast, Hopsworks) with Chalk the clear leader in published case-study throughput.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Mixed and the buyer filter is sharp. Feast Apache-2.0 (Linux Foundation governance, PyTorch Ecosystem inclusion, Red Hat-blessed). Hopsworks AGPL-v3 open-core (Community Edition AGPL is a procurement non-starter at most enterprise legal desks per Google's published AGPL Policy, Enterprise Edition paid - real open-core split). Chalk proprietary closed-source SaaS only. Tecton was proprietary, now Databricks-internal (Agent Bricks). Fennel was source-available BSL, now Databricks-internal. Redis Feature Form proprietary SaaS bundled into Redis Enterprise. Beava Apache-2.0 with no Enterprise Edition is the cleanest license posture in the segment, at parity with Feast and materially cleaner than Hopsworks/Chalk for procurement-conscious buyers - structural hedge against the Databricks/Redis bundling pressure that took out Tecton/Fennel/Featureform.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: High. The recsys feature-platform segment took the heaviest bundling hit of any feature-store sub-segment in the 2025-2026 window. Databricks alone absorbed both Tecton (Aug 2025) and Fennel (Apr 2025), folding them into Agent Bricks - any Databricks customer with a ranking model can now provision real-time feature serving from the same console as their training cluster, with offline-online parity guaranteed by the same Delta tables that already hold their training data. Databricks Lakebase ships Online Feature Stores natively for 'recommendation systems, fraud detection, and personalization engines'. Redis acquired Featureform (Oct 2025) and launched Redis Feature Form (Apr 2026) targeting exactly this segment - any Redis Enterprise customer running ElastiCache for ranking features (DoorDash, Instacart, Swiggy shape) gets a feature-store control plane bundled. SageMaker Feature Store (online on DynamoDB), Vertex AI Feature Store (Bigtable, BigQuery-native), Databricks Online Feature Store / Lakebase are all credible 'good-enough' bundles for buyers already standardised on AWS/GCP/Databricks. The recsys segment is uniquely exposed because (a) the canonical ML platform team is already on Databricks/Vertex/SageMaker for training, (b) ranking budgets are large enough to justify managed solutions, and (c) the freshness SLA is forgiving enough (seconds, not sub-second) that a slightly-slower managed feature store still meets the bar. The remaining independent addressable market is ML platform teams who explicitly do NOT want Databricks/AWS/GCP lock-in, plus mid-market live-commerce / marketplace shops where Chalk's SaaS pricing is the friction. Beava's joint TAM with Chalk/Feast/Hopsworks is shrinking each quarter.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous and segment-specific. Tier-1 recsys shops (Whatnot, Pinterest, DoorDash, Instacart, Meta) all run a Kafka event bus as the spine - Whatnot explicitly introduced Kafka into its stack to drive the home-feed ranking service; Pinterest TransAct V2 ingests 1.2M user-action events/sec; DoorDash Riviera materialises features into Redis ElastiCache from Flink. Tier-2 shops (Apartment List, Medely, the long tail of mid-market marketplaces) run application-server webhook push (HTTP) and mobile SDK direct push, often without a dedicated streaming team. Chalk accepts both Kafka and direct HTTP push; Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks/Databricks-Online-FS assume Kafka or a managed CDC pipe. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 plus framed-TCP :8081 push-on-event model fits the Apartment List / Medely / mid-market shape cleanly and works against the webhook path without a Kafka broker hop. For Whatnot/DoorDash/Pinterest-class buyers a thin Kafka/Kinesis consumer side-car is required and is not shipped in v0. Downstream consumers of the FS in this segment are the ranker (XGBoost, LightGBM, DLRM, two-tower retrieval + neural re-rankers, transformer-based sequence models like TransAct V2 at 16k actions, cross-encoder re-rankers), pulled via batch_get inside the ranking RPC. Beava's verified API surface (POST /batch_get on :8080 with heterogeneous (table, entity_id, features) requests in one frame; OP_BATCH_GET = 0x0024 on :8081) maps directly to the ranking fan-out shape - one round trip for (1 user x ~30 features) + (200 items x ~30 features) + (200 pairs x ~5 features), no N+1 calls. The published 684k EPS headline is the write-side ingest number; the corresponding p99 at recsys-shape batched-read fan-out has not been publicly benchmarked and is the highest-leverage missing artefact for this segment.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: ML scorer dominates - this is the most ML-scorer-coupled segment beava competes in. Production stacks are XGBoost/LightGBM for tabular re-ranking (Meesho, DoorDash historically, Instacart), DLRM-class deep recommender models (Meta, MLPerf 80 ms p99 server-scenario target), two-tower retrieval + neural re-rankers (Whatnot, Pinterest, TikTok Shop), transformer-based sequence models (Pinterest TransAct V2 at 16k+ lifelong actions, 160x the previous 100-action ceiling), cross-encoder rerankers for head queries. Rules engines (Drools, in-house DSL) appear only for hard business constraints (don't show this seller to this user, diversity quota, freshness cap, business-policy floors). Beava sits squarely under the ML scorer as a feature substrate, scorer-agnostic by design - the contract is batch_get(entity_ids, feature_names) -> dense vector, the same role Chalk/Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks play.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Six concrete reasons a buyer in the recsys/personalization slice would pick beava over Chalk/Feast/Hopsworks/Databricks-Online-FS today: (1) Single binary collapses the (Kafka + Flink + Redis + Feast) or (Kafka + Spark + RonDB + Hopsworks) or (Databricks Lakebase + Delta + serving endpoint) two-or-more-box norms into one process - meaningful for ML platform teams that do not have a dedicated streaming-platform team (the Apartment List, Medely, mid-market marketplace shape). (2) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives baked into the server (counters, sums, means, n_unique HLL, CMS top-K, t-digest quantile, velocity, last-N, distributions) cover exactly the recsys feature vocabulary - per-user last-N-viewed-SKU, per-item rolling CTR, per-item velocity, per-(user, category) affinity, per-item unique viewers - which is what teams currently build on top of Redis Lua / Aerospike UDFs. (3) Sub-millisecond TCP get/batch_get sits inside the 5-30 ms feature-fetch sub-budget, at parity with Chalk's sub-5 ms Apartment List number and materially faster than Vertex AI FS's ~30 ms server-side. (4) Push-on-event ingestion over HTTP/JSON :8080 plus framed-TCP :8081 without a Kafka broker requirement - works natively against the webhook / mobile-SDK direct-push patterns that mid-market live-commerce and marketplace shops actually use. (5) Apache-2.0 with no Enterprise Edition and no acquisition risk - structurally distinct from Chalk (closed-source SaaS), Hopsworks (AGPL + paid Enterprise), Tecton/Fennel/Featureform (now bundled into Databricks/Redis). (6) batch_get with heterogeneous (table, entity_id, features) requests in one frame (verified: POST /batch_get on :8080, OP_BATCH_GET = 0x0024 on :8081, results return in submission order) maps directly to the (1 user x ~30 features) + (200 items x ~30 features) + (200 pairs x ~5 features) ranking fan-out shape - no N+1 round trips. The unifying narrative is 'Redis for stateful streaming ranking features, with 60 aggregation primitives, Apache-2.0, sub-ms TCP, no Kafka required' - lands directly between Chalk's SaaS and Feast's BYO-online-store positions for mid-market live-commerce, marketplace, and personalization teams.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Concrete gaps that block production ranking deployments today, derived from use cases 6 and 18b: (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 - every managed competitor (Chalk SaaS, Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks Enterprise, Redis Feature Form, Databricks Online FS) ships TLS + IAM out of the box; this is a procurement non-starter for ML platform teams in cloud VPCs. (2) No in-process sharding - Whatnot/DoorDash/Pinterest-scale state cannot fit on one box (50-200 GB hot state at the upper edge, multi-TB at the head); single-tenant vertical-scale-only with a single point of failure. (3) No multi-region active-active replication or read-replicas - global marketplace ranking paths cannot use beava as source of truth. (4) No published batch_get benchmark at the recsys fan-out shape - the (1 user x ~30 features) + (200 items x ~30 features) + (200 pairs x ~5 features) p99 number, the artefact every buyer in this segment will demand before procurement. The 684k EPS headline is the write-side number. (5) No point-in-time-correct offline materialisation to produce training data from the same @bv.table definitions - this is the headline 'consistency' feature Hopsworks, Tecton, Chalk, Fennel, Featureform/Redis-Feature-Form all sell, and absence makes beava a 'fast online cache' rather than a full feature store in the procurement sense. (6) No vector / ANN index - modern two-tower retrieval needs an ANN side-car (Vespa, Milvus, Vald, Aerospike Vector Search, Redis Search); beava does not do retrieval, only the re-rank-stage feature serving. (7) No native embedding storage - high-dimensional vectors are not a primary-key aggregation. (8) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs - a SaaS personalization vendor cannot safely host multiple customers on one box. (9) No materialisation-from-warehouse path - Feast/Tecton/Hopsworks accept 'compute this feature in Spark nightly, write to online store' as a first-class pattern; beava expects events pushed in. (10) No SDK ergonomic for DataFrame-style online feature fetch (Feast/Tecton's get_online_features(entity_rows=DataFrame, feature_view=...) -> DataFrame); beava's batch_get is lower-level. (11) No on-demand feature transformations at request time (Tecton 'On-Demand Feature Views', Chalk 'resolvers'). (12) No feature monitoring / drift detection / per-feature distribution sketches. (13) No managed/hosted offering - buyer must operate the box themselves; Chalk, Tecton-now-Databricks, Hopsworks Serverless, Redis Feature Form, Databricks Online FS all ship managed. (14) No triggers - useful for trending-now widgets and real-time cold-start surfacing.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo. Closing the procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS + auth + namespace ACLs, items 1 and 8) is 1-3 months. Publishing the recsys-shape batch_get benchmark (item 4) is 2-4 weeks of bench work plus a recsys-rerank workload config in crates/beava-bench/configs/. Closing the differentiating-feature gaps (in-process sharding, materialisation-from-warehouse, DataFrame SDK, point-in-time-correctness contract, basic feature monitoring, on-demand resolvers, items 2/5/9/10/11/12) is another 3-9 months on top. A managed/hosted offering (item 13) is a separate quarter+ of GTM and ops work but is not strictly required for design-partner deployments with self-hosted ML platform teams - which is the realistic 'first credible recsys buyer' shape (mid-market marketplace, regional live-commerce platform, healthcare-staffing, vertical recsys SaaS).

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Mixed. Beava-side: no publicly named recsys/personalization users, no published Whatnot/Apartment-List-equivalent case study, beava.dev landing page positions as 'real-time features without heavy infrastructure'. Repo evidence is genuinely strong on the event-shape side: python/beava/demos/ecommerce/ ships PageView/AddToCart/Purchase events keyed on user_id/sku (verified schema.json), which is the canonical recsys event shape and a direct stepping-stone for a ranking demo. The verified API surface supports the ranking fan-out: POST /batch_get with heterogeneous (table, entity_id, features) per request returning results in submission order (docs/concepts/get-and-batch-get.mdx, docs/http/wire-spec.mdx); OP_BATCH_GET = 0x0024 on the framed-TCP :8081 fast-path. What is missing in the repo: an explicit 'plug beava into XGBoost/LightGBM, serve N features in one batch_get for 200 candidates' notebook (the Feast/Tecton/SageMaker demo shape), a recsys-rerank workload config in crates/beava-bench/configs/ analogous to fraud-team.json/large-with-sketches.json, and a published p99 number at the recsys fan-out shape. Competitor-side validation that the segment shape is real: Whatnot/Chalk (300M+ features/sec, P99 100 ms, 1 MB+ payloads, 65 % of GMV from feeds), Apartment List/Chalk (sub-5 ms), DoorDash Riviera + Redis ElastiCache (20M+ feature reads/sec, 1M+ predictions/sec, 23 features per prediction, Redis won internal benchmark vs Cassandra/CockroachDB/ScyllaDB/YugabyteDB), Pinterest TransAct V2 (1.2M events/sec, 16k user-action sequence per ranking call, 10 s p99 signal-to-serving), Instacart Griffin 2.0 (Flink + internal store, tripled ML application count), Hopsworks SIGMOD 2024 paper (10x p99 vs SageMaker/Vertex). Beava knows who the buyer is (ML platform team or Director of Search & Recommendations at mid-market marketplace / regional live-commerce / personalization SaaS / vertical recsys product) but has zero proof points in this segment.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - credible play, 6-12 months of focused engineering (TLS/auth + sharding + materialisation-from-warehouse + DataFrame SDK + point-in-time-correctness contract) plus a published Whatnot/Apartment-List-shaped recsys demo with paired XGBoost notebook and a recsys-rerank bench config. The wedge is genuine - single binary, 60 primitives, Apache-2.0, sub-ms TCP batch_get, no Kafka required - against a segment whose hyperscaler-bundling pressure took out three of the five prior independent vendors (Tecton, Fennel, Featureform) in twelve months. Realistic play: design-partner with one mid-market ML platform team in live-commerce or marketplace where Chalk's SaaS pricing is the friction and Databricks/Vertex lock-in is unappealing. Avoid pitching Whatnot/DoorDash/Pinterest-tier buyers until in-process sharding and multi-region replication ship - the head-tier of recsys runs on bespoke in-house feature stores and is not a winnable design-partner shape for beava in 2026. Recsys is the use case where beava's read-heavy / batch_get story is most exposed and most provable; publishing the fan-out p99 number is the single highest-leverage thing the team can do to make this segment a real wedge rather than a hopeful one.
